textRun.content: This specification describes the behaviour and visual contracts of 9to1. The editable Interface Atlas supplies the linked screen examples; this document supplies the rules, interaction outcomes and states that a still image cannot show.

This specification combines the current owner-directed interface contracts with the retained framework, runtime, app, interaction and acceptance requirements. The coverage index identifies implemented previews, specified production behaviour and any remaining source or decision gaps.

— Owner decisions take priority over older mockup notes. Preserve the latest accepted interaction and visual rules when a legacy screen still shows an earlier design. Record a conflict against its requirement and Screen ID instead of silently choosing whichever file is newest.

— A mockup is evidence of intended presentation, not evidence of a connected implementation. Examples of people, conversations, balances, providers, models and files are fixtures unless the product actually reads them from a service or local store.

— Keep three statuses distinct: Established design (explicit owner direction or a retained Atlas contract); Draft interaction (a concrete proposal for behaviour not yet settled); Preview coverage (what the offline Atlas actually demonstrates). A draft can be revised without pretending it was previously approved.
Updated 18 November 2026. The detailed interaction proposals in tab 6 are a starting specification, not a claim that all context menus have been implemented.
1.2 - Reading the specification with the mockups
Every mockup reference uses its stable Screen ID, for example
. Search that ID in the Atlas screen navigation. With the HTML open locally, appending #
to its file address opens that view directly; ?screen=

Links from this document open the Atlas file. The accompanying Screen ID identifies the exact view; it does not imply that the file-library page is a live hosted route. In the Atlas, Build notes links back to the relevant specification section.

— Keep Screen IDs stable when titles, copy or layout change. Keep compatibility routes for older saved references. Requirement IDs such as HAV-TAB-001 are stable too; add a superseding note rather than reusing an ID for a different rule.

— Each feature entry must identify its surface, trigger, visible result, state change, persistence scope, cancellation/undo path and keyboard equivalent. Link default, selected, expanded, empty, loading and failure examples when those states differ materially.
— Update the document and matching Atlas notes together. The reference index in tab 6 records the current starting coverage and the remaining interaction work.

— Use direct nouns and verbs: Settings, Appearance, Add widget, Apply and reload. Remove decorative introductions and generated-sounding taglines. Keep help text when it explains a consequence, permission, format, limit or recovery action.

— Give each visible control one job. A disclosure opens options; it does not also change a setting. Closing a menu does not commit a pending change. Navigation does not silently reset the selected model, accent, layout or conversation scope.

— Keep the primary work area quiet. Put frequent actions directly beside the work and secondary actions in labelled menus or optional panels. Consolidate repeated identity, save state and mode controls.

— Show truthful state. Pending edits, unsaved data, saving, saved, offline and failed are separate outcomes. Failure leaves recoverable input visible. A preview must not claim that an external action, permission grant, model reload or file save occurred.
— Preserve canonical identities and authored content across navigation. Changing a label, theme, layout or screen composition does not create a new Assistant, conversation or document.

— Support pointer and keyboard access to the same operations. Visible move buttons provide an alternative to drag and drop. Menus return focus to their trigger after Escape. Moving focus alone never performs a destructive action.

Global preferences follow the user across 9to1; Local preferences apply to this device. App settings reference shared preferences where relevant instead of creating competing copies. Retain the established canonical identities, revision-aware transactions, offline checkpoints, explicit replica manifests and conflict-preservation contracts. Use the retained technical chapters for exact storage and transport schemas; this design revision must not silently replace them.

CUI is the single public interface system, with Avalonia and retained donor engines as implementation details. Dulche owns the shared AI/runtime broker, routing, durable requests/TaskRuns, actions, memory and subagent integration. Preserve the v3.1 technical definitions and package contracts; current owner instructions supersede their conflicting visual presentation.

Remaining implementation and verification work includes rendered mobile layouts, the full app state matrix, native browser integration, actual model resource constraints, enforced permissions, durable collaboration and the proposed context menus. The corresponding product contracts are specified here and in the incorporated technical modules; a mockup or specification entry is not evidence that its production implementation is complete.
Cross-references: 2.1 CUI Framework; 2.3 Haven App; 3.2 Spaces Usability; 4. Boards; 5. Settings; 6. Interactions and references.

— All 9to1 surfaces use shared semantic roles for text, surfaces, borders, focus, selection and action emphasis. Native app identity artwork can keep its own colours; navigation selection and shared controls follow the chosen accent.

— Share component behaviour across apps. A tab, dropdown, toggle, menu, setting row and contextual AI bar must expose the same focus, disabled, selected, pending and dismissal states wherever they appear.

— The Professional theme uses rounded action buttons and restrained neutral containers. Large groups of controls are not each placed inside competing heavy capsules. Keep typography strong enough for messages and navigation; do not centre Haven tab content.

— A panel is optional when its information is secondary to the main task. Closing a panel preserves the underlying document, conversation and selection. Disclosures reveal existing capabilities rather than duplicating those controls elsewhere.

— The public component contract needs stable identity, semantic role, accessible name, value/state, supported actions and an explicit disabled reason when relevant. The HTML and CUI developer views must let a developer inspect the corresponding surface without confusing presentation with permission or runtime execution.
— Keep content separate from presentation. A theme or font change must not alter the canonical document text, Assistant identity, model selection or action scope.

CUI syntax and public ownership are governed by the retained technical/cui-03.md and technical/cui-04.md chapters. Generated interfaces use the safe typed component/action registry and current brokered grants; text, HTML and generated code do not acquire execution authority. The Atlas's JavaScript and DOM remain prototype implementation, not the production language definition.

— The user selects one bright accent. Primary, secondary, tertiary and ghost are emphasis treatments of that choice, not four unrelated palette colours. With blue selected, secondary navigation must not switch to purple.

— Primary actions use the strongest accent treatment. Secondary actions and selected sub-sections use a softer treatment of the same hue. Tertiary and ghost actions keep quieter surfaces while retaining clear hover, focus and selected states. Semantic error/warning/success colours remain distinct from decorative accent choice.

— Accent previews show the shared action treatments together. Light/Dark uses the same rounded segmented-control language as the rest of the Professional theme. The selected segment is evident through shape/contrast and state, not colour alone.

— Messages and navigation use a stronger weight than decorative metadata. Haven tabs are left aligned with stable icon, title and close positions; only the Main/Voice/Vision selector is centred within its own tab segments.

— Scrollbars inherit the current surface and theme. Keep a visible usable thumb, transparent or matching track, and stronger contrast in high-contrast mode. Do not hide overflow to disguise a pale edge or clipped layout.

Acceptance: choose blue, navigate through Home, Settings, model picker, Assistants and Boards, then reopen the file. Shared selected controls retain blue emphasis and a readable focus state; authored artwork is preserved.

Dulche is the canonical shared AI/runtime broker described in the retained v3.1 Dulche technical chapters. It owns model routing, request admission/execution, durable TaskRuns and ActionGraphs, tool actions, memory and subagent integration. Haven hosts the surfaces and CUI defines the public UI; neither introduces a competing execution or state authority. Preserve existing API, transport, multi-engine and embedded-service contracts while applying the current presentation changes.

— Haven owns the outer tab strip, address/navigation row, model picker and shared utilities. Embedded apps do not repeat an entire Home/account/history/chat header. App-specific actions remain in the host or a compact app toolbar where they are meaningful.
— Home and New tab are one customisable start surface. There is no fixed Home tab. New tab appears below Explore in the Home sidebar and remains available from the tab-strip plus button.

— A normal Haven tab contains its icon, left-aligned bold title and visible close X. Selecting a Home sidebar destination changes the active tab's content/title while preserving its close control and tab identity. A close control has an accessible name and is separately focusable from the navigation target.
— Closing Home/New tab selects the nearest valid tab to the right, then to the left; if none remains, open
and focus the active tab. Draft extension: reopening a recently closed tab restores its route and recoverable state. Do not discard unsaved document edits without the app's save/recovery contract.

— Draft tab context menu: New tab; Reload; Duplicate; Pin/Unpin; Mute/Unmute when audio exists; Move to another window when supported; Close; Close others; Close tabs to the right; Reopen closed tab. Disable inapplicable items and keep destructive groups separated. See CTX-01 in tab 6.

Preview boundary: the functional native Close control currently covers shared Home/New tab and Home sidebar destinations. Other legacy work-tab X icons remain visual examples; general tab closing/reopening still needs implementation.

Acceptance: open New tab, choose Apps then Models then Assistants from the sidebar, and close the active tab. The X stays present, routes remain correct and focus moves to the resulting active tab. Repeat with a saved/edited Atlas screen.
— The start surface has search, optional clock/date, pinned shortcuts and widgets. Home and New tab share layout, background, visibility, width and order preferences. Older
references resolve to the same surface.

— Customise is a visual editing mode. Drag handles appear on editable tiles; move buttons and keyboard alternatives operate on the same order. The editor previews layouts, backgrounds and available widgets instead of presenting only text toggles.

— Adding, moving, switching a widget between compact and wide, or removing it changes layout metadata. Preserve its authored body and source identity. Reordering shortcuts never rewrites their targets. Done leaves the editor; Reset layout restores the declared defaults and has a recovery/undo path.

— Search and Ask AI are separate actions. Search navigation must distinguish a supported page or address from an unsupported preview target. Failed resolution leaves the user's input visible and states the problem beside the field.
— The scroll area stays inside the content region without a bright unexplained side line. At narrow widths, controls wrap and tiles stack without horizontal page overflow or obscuring the sidebar.

— Draft context menus reuse the visible editor's move/remove actions and compact/wide widget choices. Edit shortcut label/target and widget-specific Configure are additional proposed flows; they are not yet demonstrated by the editor. Removing a shortcut/widget does not delete its source app, file or event.
Preview boundary: drag/move/width/visibility choices and supported Atlas navigation are demonstrated. Calendar, note, activity and timer data are sample content; no live external source is implied.
— The picker contains centred Main, Voice and Vision tabs. This alignment is scoped to the picker; Haven's own tabs remain left aligned.

— Within a role, Reasoning stays visible. Context, Model and Assistant/Specialist are separate collapsible headings that show the current selection or status while closed; Context can show usage or Pending changes. Use one compact searchable list of model rows with name, short source label and selected state.

— Distinguish local device, remote app/device and cloud provider sources without repeating the same source description in large stacked cards. Browse models opens the model catalogue. Preserve a role's current choice when another section opens or the role tab changes.

— Changing Context creates a pending value. Show Apply and reload only when it differs from the applied value. Typing, Enter, dismissing a section or switching roles must not silently apply it. Invalid values leave the applied value unchanged and show an inline reason.

— The production implementation must validate a context limit against the selected model/provider and available resources. Do not infer a maximum from sample numbers. Applying starts an explicit reload operation; show loading, success or failure, and retain recoverable input if reload fails.

— Assistant/Specialist selection references canonical identities shared with Home and Spaces. Selecting None removes that participant choice for the role; it does not delete the underlying Assistant or Specialist.

Preview boundary: Apply and reload stores the chosen context and redraws the offline view. It does not reload a real inference runtime. The preview shares one pending/applied context value across Main, Voice, Vision and the host context popup, saved as uiPreferences.modelContextTokens. Model, reasoning and participant selections are per-role in-session state and are not saved-file preferences. Production provider limits still need implementation.
2.3.4 - Browser tools, Manage page and inspectors

— Browser tools is a compact command menu with engine, developer tools, history, bookmarks, reload and settings. Use normal command labels and submenus; do not replace the menu with long instructions about another browser.

— Manage page describes the current page: origin/address, protocol and connection status, page-specific permissions and storage/site controls where supported. Separate an internal 9to1 page from an HTTPS site or insecure origin. Display the actual state; do not claim a security property from a decorative icon.

— Permission changes are scoped to the displayed origin and permission. Show Ask/Allow/Block or the applicable supported states, plus Reset permissions. An unavailable capability remains explained and cannot silently broaden access.

— HTML and CUI developer tools expose a tree, selection properties and a console area. The view clearly identifies which representation is being inspected. Selecting an item updates the corresponding properties without editing the source by default.

— History and bookmarks have distinct views and actions. Reload acts on the current page. Changing the browser engine is an explicit preference whose production implementation must handle unavailable engines and any required reload.
. Browser tools and Manage page are available from the host controls.

Preview boundary: the current inspectors show a bounded read-only snapshot and a query-only console. They do not evaluate arbitrary JavaScript. Engine and permission controls are preview preferences; native engines, certificates and operating-system grants are not changed.

— Use one bold, legible contextual prompt with an access dropdown. Read-only and Take actions are explicit options, not a cycling button. The menu displays the current choice and restores focus when dismissed.

AI-BAR-002 — Settings → Appearance → Layout owns Chat bar position: Off, Floating or Sidebar. Position is a presentation preference. It does not grant actions, disable auditing or change a conversation's permission scope. Preserve specific app placement contracts: CANVAS-002 keeps Canvas's AI tool in its single options host; this preference must not create a second composer or remove that tool.

— The current document's View/Edit mode, layout lock and AI access are separate controls. Take actions cannot override a read-only document or a denied capability. A proposed consequential change still follows the relevant review/approval flow.

— Keep one contextual AI entry point in an editor. Avoid an additional toolbar AI button that duplicates the bottom/side bar. Spaces' conversation permission control is a different concept and remains available in its composer.

— A Space is a task environment with its conversation, relevant sources, tools, permissions and outputs. An Assistant is a persistent identity that can appear in a Space; changing the view does not create a copy of that identity or its conversation.

— Main and secondary Assistant conversations keep independent thread identity under the same Assistant. A rename or portrait change updates presentation without replacing the canonical identity. A shared conversation remains the same object wherever it opens.

— Scope belongs to the selected conversation/Assistant and authorised resources. Team membership does not grant access to another Assistant's private memory or every file in the workspace. Sources and generated outputs retain their own identities and access boundaries.

— Runs, proposals, approvals and saved results are distinct. Opening a proposed change or a review page does not approve it. A user can inspect the scope, pending action and resulting artifact before an operation proceeds.

— Make the conversation the primary reading area. Use one compact identity header, readable semibold messages and restrained vertical spacing. Avoid repeating the same title, model, privacy label and context chips across header, sidebar and composer.

— Keep conversation navigation, creation and discovery in the sidebar. Secondary navigation groups may collapse. A selected Assistant stays clearly identifiable by the same name and portrait used in the roster and response attribution.

— The workspace/source panel is optional. A clear Workspace control opens it and indicates its expanded state. Closing it preserves messages, scroll position, selected conversation and scope. On narrower layouts, it must not squeeze the conversation into an unusable column.

— Composer controls provide attachments, input, voice/send as appropriate and a direct conversation permissions entry. Do not show literal HTML resize handles or implementation markup. Wrapping and scroll behaviour must keep the composer usable without overlapping a disclaimer or message.

— Message actions appear beside the targeted message or in its menu. Draft commands include Copy, Copy link, Edit user message, Retry assistant response, Save output and Delete where allowed. See CTX-04; editing/retrying must disclose whether it creates a branch or replaces downstream history before that policy is implemented.

— Empty, loading, offline, permission denied and failed response states keep the user's draft intact. A collapsed panel or menu never hides a blocking approval or converts a proposal into an applied change.

Acceptance: open each Assistant, toggle Workspace, open conversation permissions and return. The same conversation, authored text, portrait, proposal links and source scope remain available; only secondary presentation changes.

The subsections below identify the existing Space types and their linked starting views. Detailed workflow requirements beyond the Assistant refinement remain incomplete; sample content should not be read as a separate production promise.

— The general Agent conversation supports user input, attachments, visible activity and linked artifacts. A task run exposes its current status and any proposed action requiring review. Separate the user-facing activity summary from private implementation details.

— Coordinated subagents have visible task ownership and limited scope. Their presence does not imply access to unrelated private files. Link a generated file to its canonical app/document rather than embedding an untracked competing copy.

— The Assistants Space and Home catalogue expose the same persistent identities. My Assistants, Teams and creation/configuration lead to the relevant existing destinations; these are not separate sets of assistants.

— A conversation has one compact Assistant identity header. Keep response attribution and the selected sidebar entry, but remove redundant large headings and repeated composer chips. Display the actual message text without rewriting authored conversation content during a layout change.

— Workspace contains conversations, sources, tools and memory scope. It opens on demand. Configuration and secondary operations live behind labelled controls; conversation permissions stay directly reachable from the composer.

— Main is permanent. Draft menus may rename, pin/unpin or archive a secondary thread; they must not offer a misleading operation that removes Main or deletes the Assistant. Deleting an Assistant is a separate clearly named operation with a stated effect on its conversations and memory.

— Preserve proposals and approval links. An Assistant describing a plan is not proof that a Planner event or file was changed. Context filtering, team visibility and panel collapse affect presentation only.
Context-menu detail: CTX-03 (Assistant/thread), CTX-04 (message), CTX-05 (source). Configuration and persistence beyond the demonstrated controls still need implementation coverage.
— Research separates the question, plan, source scope, run state and outputs. Outside-web access is an explicit source-scope choice. A selected budget is not a guaranteed completion time.

— Keep citations and missing-evidence information with the output. A report opens as a canonical document in the appropriate app. Do not display a finished report or completed progress before that output exists.

— Shopping separates requirements, comparison, sourced findings and any later consequential action. Comparison fixtures are not current prices or availability. Purchasing and external account actions require their own explicit, reviewable flow.
. Product search, current offers, checkout and purchase recovery remain to be specified.

— Translation keeps source content, target language and output distinguishable. Users can revise the request and copy or save the result without losing the original. Locale and formatting decisions must be explicit when they change meaning.
. Detailed language selection, file handling and error states remain to be specified.
Status: retained product contract, with the current compact visual treatment. These requirements extend the existing Spaces section; they do not introduce another runtime.

— Preserve the canonical conversation, editable draft, text selection, reading position, attachment references, voice session and active Task/Run when switching Space or hiding a sidebar. Revalidate resources against the destination scope; unavailable attachments remain explainable rather than silently receiving broader access.

— The compact composer expands upward for a nonempty/focused draft. Aa and native Unicode emoji appear only in the expanded focused state. Emoji insertion edits the current selection without sending. Attachment/resource discovery distinguishes Files, Skills, Plugins & Apps, Specialists and Assistants; attaching or mentioning a capability does not execute it.

— Keep draft text until request admission succeeds. Validation, unavailable models, denied scope or a full queue leaves the draft and attachment context recoverable. Assign the admitted request its own identity; displaying a response bubble or pressing a shelf arrow is not admission.

— Idle exposes Send and Voice; an empty disabled Send does not disable Voice. Running work exposes only supported Steer, Stop, Queue and Voice actions. Preserve the existing per-Space Steer/Queue default and documented Alt+Enter inversion. Steer applies to future work; Queue creates a separate pending message. Neither rewrites immutable prior user input or implicitly approves a tool action.

— Stop acknowledges the actual runtime boundary, preserves committed work and does not promise to reverse completed external actions. Paused, waiting for input, awaiting approval, cancelled, completed and failed have different state-specific controls. A reopened view attaches to the existing run without resubmitting it.

— If the user scrolls up, streaming must preserve that reading position. Offer an explicit return-to-latest affordance. Optional Summary shows Activity, Outputs and Sources without becoming a permanent fourth column. Activity contains observed steps and tool/status events; it does not expose private reasoning or invent progress percentages.

— Conversation permissions narrow durable grants. Cancel leaves scope unchanged; Save applies to future requests and cannot retroactively authorise past work. Approval identifies the exact proposed action, canonical target/revision, scope and consequence. Recheck policy at execution; a reviewed plan authorises only its declared scope. Every AI mutation in Data retains its stricter per-action approval requirement.

Acceptance: type and attach, switch Space and return, reject admission, then admit one request. While running, scroll up, steer, queue, stop and reconnect. Verify retained input, one request/run lineage, truthful pending work and no replay of committed effects. Open/cancel/save permissions and confirm the actual effective grant, not merely its icon.
Sources: V3-SPACES-LAY-01–13; V3-SPACES-FEA-01–04; V3-SPACES-PER-01,05–07; V3-PERMISSIONS-FEA-01–04; V3-PERMISSIONS-PER-01; Atlas screen notes for the listed routes;
3.5 - Conversation types, organisation and Space configuration

Status: retained product contract. Several creation/conversion and Builder states are specified in the baseline but have no dedicated current Atlas screen; do not substitute a fictitious implemented preview.

— Chat Type and Chat Location are independent. Types are Normal, Multi-Agent and Temporary; storage locations are Local, Mesh and Cloud. Model execution location is a separate policy-controlled choice. Local conversation storage does not claim local inference.

— Preserve the approved conversions Temporary→Normal, Temporary→Multi-Agent and Normal→Multi-Agent without replaying tools or fabricating earlier participant replies. Temporary first becomes durable local history; promotion to Mesh/Cloud is separate. Temporary chats do not automatically create/reinforce durable memory or transfer remotely. Optional reads of existing memory remain a recorded unresolved policy, not an inferred permission.

— Group and Project organise canonical conversations; they are neither Multi-Agent conversations nor new Spaces. Group adds scoped shared instructions/context; Project additionally has Sources, Rules and resource connections. Group→Project is supported while preserving identity/history/members where safe. Project→Group is rejected. Removing either container does not silently delete its member conversations.

— Context compaction preserves complete original message/output history. Summaries are derived records with source provenance and eligibility. They cannot become a replacement history or confer access to excluded source content.

— Space Override → User Preference → Default governs configuration, bounded by current policy. Locked values show their source. Basic, Advanced and Expert are projections of one SpaceID and Draft/Active revision, not competing configuration stores.

— Basic contains identity, instructions, resources and supported capability categories. Advanced adds Mandatory/Allowed/Blocked/Inherited capability policy, memory, actual model parameters, canonical Assistant/Specialist and Automation references, and theme/sidebar/message overrides. Expert reuses the shared Node Editor for Harness Logic, Model Logic, User Message Logic and nested Files. User Message Logic transforms derived representations while retaining the original message.

— Switching Builder views preserves Expert-only nodes and flags configurations that simpler views cannot express. Preview, Validate and Activate/Create are distinct. Invalid dependencies, typed ports, cycles/budgets or mandatory-but-blocked conflicts cannot replace the valid active graph. Imported packages retain owner/version/trust; folder membership does not activate them.

Acceptance: verify each supported/rejected conversion; remove an organisation container without losing its chats; compact context without deleting history; switch all Builder projections after adding Expert-only logic; reject invalid activation and retain the prior active revision.
. Builder and conversion workflows require additional dedicated mockups; their retained behaviour remains binding meanwhile.
3.6 - Task-specific Spaces and learning entry points
Status: retained contracts that complement the detailed app sections. Domain artifacts remain owned by their apps, with stable references from Spaces.

— Tasks shows the current user's relevant task scope by default, with explicit All Tasks filtering. Its objective, plan, dependencies, blockers, approvals, sources, outputs and summary are views of the same Action Graph. A queued request is not an active task, and a completed preparation step is not an accepted output.

— Research begins with a conversation, then exposes a reviewable plan, permitted sources, budget and selected deliverables before Start. Quick/Extended/Deep/Custom represent supported budgets; active execution time excludes waiting/paused periods and is not a completion guarantee. Outside-web access never broadens itself. Findings retain citations and gaps; the final report is a canonical Write artifact.

— Shopping separates Required from Preferred constraints and strict matches from near matches/alternatives and contextual recommendations. Keep mismatch reasons visible. Products and merchant offers are different entities; currency, price, source and last-check state accompany offers. Save, Compare and Purchase are distinct operations; selection or a recommendation cannot authorise purchase.

— Translate stays conversational. Language chips sit above the standard composer; each target has its own labelled response bubble. Variants are siblings of one TranslationSet. Refining one language preserves the other variants and the source. Replacing/publishing source content requires the owning app's separate authorised action.

— Experiences stores canonical world/scene, character, inventory, evidence, objective, flag and checkpoint state. Validate and commit a transition before narrating its outcome. A checkpoint branch preserves both matching conversation and world-state revision and keeps the original timeline. Rewind cannot undo completed external actions. Hidden character knowledge and clues must not leak through side panels or generated UI. Formal contestants, rounds and scoring belong to Play.

— Study Home, Subject Workspace and Session are distinct active views within the same Space. Opening a subject/session replaces the active work area, not a dashboard laid over a hidden editor. Modes Learn, Practise, Test and Review preserve conversation/topic/source policy and draft. Cards, Forms and Planner open their canonical artifacts, then return to the same Study context. The learning chapter owns evidence, proficiency, ranking and assessment rules; time spent, opening a lesson or flipping a card is not mastery.

Acceptance: Research cannot start an unreviewable plan; Shopping keeps a Required mismatch visible; Translate edits one variant without replacing siblings; Experiences restores a consistent branch; Study opens a real Cards/Forms artifact and returns without duplicate records. Failure in one output does not erase other completed work.
Sources: V3-SPACES-FEA-09–15,21–22; V3-SPACES-ENT-05; V3-SPACES-ACC-04,10; Atlas Experiences and Translate current screen notes;
3.7 - Subagents, generated UI and durable outputs
Status: retained product contract. Current interactive examples demonstrate presentation and selected local transitions, not connected execution.

— A subagent has a stable parent Task/Run relationship, objective, identity/route, delegated inputs, allowed outputs, current state, budget and output references. Its grant is the intersection of parent permission, agent capability and current policy. Enforce delegation depth/concurrency/budget limits; spawning another worker cannot bypass exhaustion or a required review.

— Structured joins retain each child's outcome. Cancel/retry/review is scoped to the selected task; a failed child does not delete completed sibling artifacts. Reconnect to existing runs rather than launch duplicates. Configured Assistants/Teams remain distinct from generic worker delegation; preserve canonical identities when they participate.

— Generated UI uses validated CUI component/action schemas. Model text or arbitrary HTML is not automatically trusted executable UI. Controls bind to authorised source entities and retain selection/input across streaming updates. Invalid generated output leaves previous valid content recoverable and exposes repair.

— An ephemeral proposal is distinct from a promoted durable artifact. A planner slider edits the proposal; Save to Planner opens the exact change review. Live Present/Canvas work shows the owning app's actual scene, revision, selection and responsible collaborator. Open in App retains that artifact/session and history, not a copied representation.

— A finished result requires an owning-app durable artifact receipt. Show name, owning app, canonical ID/revision, native/export type and actual local/sync state. Open resolves the existing artifact; Download requires verified existing bytes. Neither silently repeats generation.

— Export failure is scoped to the chosen export. Retain the saved native source, format/options, target, source revision, error and targeted Retry/Save copy actions. A retry rechecks current grants and idempotency; uncertain external outcomes require reconciliation before repetition. Never show Ready or Download for an absent/incomplete file.

Acceptance: run two children with mixed outcomes, revoke one scope, reconnect and verify no duplicate execution. Change a generated control, reject invalid schema, open the canonical artifact, then force a secondary export failure. Preserve completed work, source identity, revision and valid prior UI.
Sources: V3-SUBAGENTS-LAY-01–02; V3-SUBAGENTS-FEA-01–03; V3-SUBAGENTS-ENT-01–02; V3-SUBAGENTS-PER-01–02; V3-GENERATIVE-UI-FEA-01–04; V3-GENERATIVE-UI-ENT-01–02; V3-GENERATIVE-UI-PER-01–02;

— A Board contains sections/pages with stable identities. The sidebar owns the board switcher, page tree, undo/redo and save state. Selecting a page opens that same canonical page; it does not duplicate its content.

— Use one seamless native page where flow blocks, explicitly positioned content and page ink can coexist. Preserve the authored document while changing surrounding chrome. A design refinement must not rewrite text, callouts, lists, tables, drawings or their order.

— Keep the page itself the focus. Remove duplicated board/save labels and a separate decorative mode row. The toolbar contains frequent actions once; repeated Native page, locked-layout and snapping labels belong in the relevant Page menu.

— Use one compact toolbar with direct Add, Drawing, Edit/View and Collaborate controls. Format opens the original text/paragraph/font/list/alignment controls. Page opens Properties, layout lock, snapping and the original page options.

— Format and Page are real disclosures. The active trigger announces its expanded state. Escape and outside click close a popup; keyboard navigation reaches every enabled control and returns focus appropriately. Opening one popup closes an overlapping sibling.

— Preserve the original actions behind their new grouping. Reorganising chrome does not remove styling, drawing, properties, page options or collaboration. The redundant toolbar AI entry is removed because the contextual AI bar already owns that entry point.

— Name sidebar creation clearly: New page creates a page/section; toolbar Add and block insertion create content within the current page. The board-name control opens file actions; renaming is an explicit command, not a side effect of opening the switcher.

— View/Edit, layout lock and AI access are separate dimensions. View mode prevents document edits. Layout lock restricts layout manipulation while retaining the established page-ink behaviour. Take actions cannot bypass either permission or read-only restrictions.

— A block grip identifies one block. Click selects; dragging begins only after a deliberate movement threshold. A context menu uses the explicit target/selection and does not silently switch to an unrelated page or block.

— The block menu, overflow button and keyboard menu command expose the same applicable actions. Preserve selection and return focus after cancellation. For multiple blocks, show only actions that apply to the whole selection or state why they are unavailable.

— The existing Paragraph actions view contains Turn into, Colour & style, Move up/down, Move to…, Duplicate, Copy block link and Delete block. Draft additions are Copy, Cut and Comment where appropriate. Preserve those established actions and use the existing menu/insert views as the visual starting point. Read-only, locked, empty-selection and protected-content states determine availability.

— Draft page-tree menu: Open, Open in new tab, Rename, Duplicate, Move, Copy link, Export and Delete. Draft canvas menu: Paste, Insert block, Drawing, Select all, Properties and Layout controls. Exact ordering and app-specific extensions are recorded in CTX-06 to CTX-08.

— Saved locally, saving, unsaved and save failure are distinct. File actions retain the original board name and location context. Save As creates an editable .9to1board in an allowed location; a failed save does not replace the last recoverable content.

— Draft deletion is undoable where the data model permits. Show the affected page/block count. Deleting a page with descendants or an unrecoverable external change needs a specific consequence and recovery decision; do not use a generic confirmation for every harmless operation.

Acceptance: open the normal editor and each menu/state view. The authored board content is identical, frequent actions remain direct, formatting/page controls are reachable once, and there is one save-state source in the sidebar.

Acceptance: open Format then Page, cancel with Escape, switch Edit/View, inspect Properties, draw with the layout locked and follow the existing save-recovery route. Record which actions the offline preview demonstrates and which require the production editor.
— Use a three-tier hierarchy: collapsible text Group; icon/text Section; indented Sub-section in the secondary treatment of the selected accent. Group collapse is separate from section navigation.

Stream an invalid generated component, recover, promote valid output and verify Open/Download reference the same saved source revision.

Retained baseline: the recovered source pack contains the full language/API contracts. The following are implementation gates, not illustrative alternative designs. Read the complete chapters before changing parser, runtime or security code.

— The ten visual/structural primitives are Page, Container, Text, Image, Audio, Video, Object, Button, Input and Layer. Extend through registered Type, Definition, Prefab or Object Type. CUI is a strict XML-like language; built-in keywords are case-insensitive and user symbols case-sensitive. Preserve typed properties, scoped ID/Name and Groups, imports, events, conditions, live Repeat, styles, theme inheritance and the declared compiler pipeline. Reject unknown/ambiguous syntax and production donor markup.

— Preserve Text as literal content and Children as deliberately parsed, capability-limited markup. Invalid Children updates retain the last valid tree. Static Prefabs share internal runtime state, dynamic Prefabs do not; neither implies persistence. Active, Hidden and Interactive remain independent. Live bindings use dependency notification rather than per-frame polling. Compiled output records language version, runtime ABI/registry version and required capabilities. Inspectors expose winning property sources and dependency/accessibility state.

— Preserve documented API names, argument order and Result fields. RequestID is assigned before queueing; SessionID owns context, EndpointID identifies logical execution and port/URL identifies transport. A shared endpoint never means shared session. Retain Dulche.Start(port), Test(port), Prompt(request, endpoint), SetModel(model, port), Pause(port) and Stop(port), together with documented overloads. Request-ID controls never broadcast; endpoint-wide omitted-port commands remain confined to the caller's authorised scope.

— Preserve the configurable engine abstraction/dispatcher and public setInferenceEngine/getInferenceEngine contract. Automatic selection filters incompatibility before measured fit; incompatible manual selection fails explicitly. The retained source describes llama.cpp and Strata; treat Strata-specific interfaces as compatibility/history in light of the later owner plan to replace it. That plan names Thunder for MoE and Lightning for dense/llama.cpp, with Monstrosity also mentioned; exact adapter mapping and migration require repository confirmation. Do not describe those engines as already integrated or hard-code Strata as the required future backend.

— Persistent requests retain one RootRequestID, CompletionContract, dependency graph, attempt lineage, SteeringMessages, blockers and completed-action receipts across continuation boundaries. A progress report is not completion evidence. Stop remains cancellation; it must not auto-resume. Continue independent runnable work when one node is blocked, and use AwaitingUser only when the remaining work requires input.

— Context compaction is a derived execution view over durable history. Preserve obligations, permissions, identifiers/revisions, completed actions, evidence and unresolved conflicts. Context Summarisation uses bounded, provenance-preserving passes when ordinary compaction is insufficient. Cloud summarisation requires its own applicable disclosure grant; otherwise expose a non-destructive capacity blocker. Preserve Context.Compact, Context.Summarise and Context.GetState contracts.

— Derive a request-specific EffectiveCapabilitySet from the canonical Tool Registry. Resolve semantic intent and typed multi-tool plans before claiming inability; distinguish missing capability, unavailable capability, prerequisites and policy denial. Computer Use requires explicit invocation/control and retains its separate approval and excluded-target rules. It is not an automatic fallback when an app API fails.

— UCML is a versioned context representation with provenance, owner, scope, consent, retention and security metadata. It is not encryption. Keep keys, credentials and raw authentication secrets in trusted key management; never inject them into models. The scoped Context Broker returns only authorised relevant context. Rotation preserves decryptability of legitimately retained data; closed-source packaging is not the security boundary.

Acceptance: run the retained CUI conformance suite against real app surfaces; test cross-session isolation, scoped endpoint broadcasts, manual-engine incompatibility, persistent restart/steering/Stop, cloud-summary denial and semantic capability resolution. Verify that context and diagnostic outputs contain no key material and that invalid markup cannot gain execution authority.
: V2-B2248..B2261, COMPANION-B0084/SPUI-194; Later owner context: 16 November engine direction, supplied by root; repository confirmation pending.

— Retained baseline: each owning app keeps its canonical artifact, stable object IDs, current revision and undo history. Shared menus, theme, model picker and collaboration project that same state. Opening a document from Home, Files, Boards, Study, Link or an Assistant must resolve the original rather than create an untracked copy.

— Follow the latest Haven integration: one outer tab system and one source of document identity/save state. Do not reintroduce an app's duplicate file tabs or host utility row because an older screen note lists them. App-specific menus and contextual controls remain available; dragging a file between Haven tabs must preserve its identity and disclose the actual operation.

— For Write, Present and Canvas, Start is a separate view with New, Open, Import, Templates and Recent. Direct-open/session restore bypasses Start; returning to Start retains the existing document session. Missing files, unsupported imports and partially recovered artifacts have explicit recovery states. A recent-file entry is a reference, not proof of local availability.

— Authored fonts, colours, charts, images, ink and geometry are document values. A UI theme/accent change affects chrome and selected controls without recolouring the document. Legacy per-app accent notes are superseded for shared control emphasis; recognisable app icons may retain their artwork colours.

— Every implementation slice needs default, selection, editing, loading, empty, denied, offline and failure states where applicable. Preserve recoverable drafts on failure. Distinguish saving a project, exporting a representation, sharing access and executing an external action; none may be used as a misleading substitute for another.

— Draft interaction standard: the context menu and toolbar invoke the same command implementation, with identical target, permissions and undo transaction. Text fields retain useful native editing behaviour. Commands that depend on selection, media, clipboard, project status or platform capability are disabled with a reason rather than producing fictional success.

— This chapter is a current interaction/readout layer over the complete retained modules and their technical clauses. Unpictured capabilities remain requirements; catalogue entries and mockup buttons are not backend completion evidence. Ordinary local authoring remains usable without sign-in, Files or a running AI model unless that operation actually requires one. Context-menu lists marked Draft are implementation proposals under the shared command/permission rules, not evidence of earlier approval.

Acceptance: create/open an artifact, change view and theme, open it from another app, return, undo an edit and reopen the saved file. Identity, authored content and revision history remain consistent. Use the app-specific rules below where they impose stricter boundaries.
Sources: Atlas LAUNCH-001–006; UX27-HOST-001–006; current owner Haven integration instructions, 18 November 2026;

— Pages, Continuous and Book are views of one DocumentID, section tree, comments, selection and revision. New native documents default to Continuous unless a template requires pagination; restored documents retain their view. Page View has real authored margins and page geometry. Continuous is one flowing reading surface without paper cards, shadows or artificial inter-sheet gaps.

— Continuous retains page-aware semantics: section/page breaks, margins, headers, footnotes and pagination. A real break has a quiet marker rather than an invented sheet. Sections are authored nodes; headings derive from heading styles. Outline collapse, width and scroll are user view state and must preserve the caret and selection.

— The caret, selected range, toolbar and Properties share one editing state. User Edit/Suggest/View, layout Locked/Unlocked and AI Read-only/Take actions are independent. The contextual AI area reserves usable space; text and status controls never paint behind it. Authored formatting survives display mode and UI-theme changes.

— Suggest mode anchors a pending change to the exact range. Accept commits the selected change as an undoable operation after revision/scope checks; Dismiss rejects it without changing unrelated content. Comments are separate from edits and retain stable anchors when their section moves. The review panel scrolls independently and can reveal the precise target without covering it.

— Collaborators use the same global Assistant/Specialist identity and document revision. Invitations state source/range scope and operation mode; Invite begins work, while accepting a proposal is a separate operation. Pause/Stop retain task history and already committed edits. A stale proposed change requires revalidation rather than silent last-writer-wins.

— Retain the full rich-text engine: paragraph/character styles, nested sections, tables, positioned objects, references/fields, review, native documents, foreign-format compatibility, PDF opening/editing and derived export. Preserve supported donor features and report conversion limitations explicitly; a quiet toolbar does not reduce document capability.

Draft context menus: selection offers Cut, Copy, Paste where available, formatting, Link, Comment and Suggest; a suggestion offers Accept/Dismiss; an outline item offers Navigate, Rename heading and section operations that the current mode permits. Source text, comment, heading and suggestion targets must stay distinct.

Acceptance: switch Continuous→Pages→Book→Continuous with a selected range and pending suggestion; confirm unchanged content and comment anchors. Move a section, reveal its comment, reject one suggestion and accept another; one Undo restores the accepted change only. Test inaccessible collaborator scope and interrupted save without losing the draft.
Sources: WRITE-UX-101–120; UX27-WRITE-001–007; Atlas owner revision: true Continuous view; Atlas global collaborator contracts;

— Preserve the presentation's stable slide/object IDs, source revision and slide order. Within Haven, consolidate duplicate identity chrome while retaining conventional app menus and exactly one contextual toolbar. Insert and Actions remain visible entry points. Fit uses the central viewport remaining after Notes/Properties and never allows a 16:9 slide to overflow into controls.

— Single click selects; double click or Enter edits text. Eight resize handles and rotation follow object geometry and are transient overlays, excluded from export. Slide Notes has its own resize edge and scroll area. Bottom-right zoom provides minus, slider, actual derived percentage, plus and icon-only Fit; panel changes must recalculate the displayed transform.

— Insert opens a catalogue. Choosing Shapes opens the shared gallery without allocating an object. The custom-shape builder holds an uncommitted draft; Insert shape creates one editable canonical shape, while Cancel restores the caller's insertion context without leaving a stray object.

— Transitions is a simple editor over the same canonical Actions graph, not a separate animation engine. A preset changes only its owned subgraph. Open in Actions reveals that graph; user extension nodes outside the owned region survive simple edits. Nonrepresentable advanced edits show Custom/Advanced instead of being approximated or deleted.

— Actions target stable slide/object IDs. A navigation request commits once and has explicit completion/failure. Authoring interactions do not trigger playback. Runtime preview is deliberate, with transient state kept separate from the document; typed failures and event budgets belong to the shared runtime.

— Presenter view is private: notes, next slide and elapsed time are excluded from audience output by default. Leaving playback restores authoring state. Session ink remains separate from permanent content unless explicitly committed. Variants is an integrated comparison surface: identify source/base/target revisions, preview selected semantic changes and refresh stale conflicts before merge; switching/merging never publishes or presents.

— Retain layouts/masters, text/media, object alignment/arrangement, animation, keyboard nudge and proportional resize. Collaborators target the same deck/selected slide with expected revisions and typed reviewable changes. Playback grants no new write or external-action authority; failed export retains the native deck.

Draft context menus: slide thumbnail offers New, Duplicate, Reorder, Hide/Show, Notes, Transition and Delete; object offers Copy/Duplicate, Arrange, Group where valid, Properties, Actions and Delete. Visibility changes and destructive commands respect selection/mode and are undoable.

Acceptance: open Notes and Properties, Fit the slide, edit one object, create/cancel a custom shape and reopen its builder. Edit Fade in the simple panel and inspect the same graph; preserve an extension node. Present to an audience view and verify notes/selection handles are absent. Merge a stale variant only after refreshed comparison.
Sources: PRESENT-UX-101–106; PRESENT-DES-201–207; PRESENT-INT-101–107/201–202; TF-V01–03; Atlas Actions/Transitions and collaboration contracts;

— Canvas uses one coordinate model for drawing, hit testing, selection and viewport transforms. Infinite mode fills the viewport without an artificial paper edge. Object, layer and stroke identities survive zoom/pan, cross-app insertion and save/reopen. UI themes do not change authored background, stroke or fill colours.

— The bottom-centre primary tool order is Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI; only the selected tool shows its label. Reselecting Pen opens deeper preset options. One options host sits above the tools; AI replaces that host instead of creating a second permanently expanded composer. Layers is an explicit popup for selected-object work, not a permanently reserved rail.

— Insert's first-level categories are Text, Shapes, Media, Table and Other. Opening a category allocates nothing until a choice is committed. Pen presets resolve properties onto new strokes so later preset changes do not rewrite old strokes. Pressure/tilt options reflect device capability; mouse input retains a usable fixed-width fallback.

— Present and Canvas share the editable shape/path model. Anchors, segments, closed state and fill rule persist. Corner, Smooth and Symmetric alter tangent constraints; linked Bézier handles, numeric coordinates, add/remove/split, keyboard nudge and Boolean operations use coherent undo transactions. Preview excludes selection adorners.

— Save to My shapes stores a reusable definition; inserting an instance keeps editable geometry. Cancel discards only the uncommitted builder draft. Source permissions and caller selection remain intact when returning to an app.

— Retain grouping, connectors, transforms, drawing/erasing and supported hybrid raster/vector operations. Semantic AI edits target actual selected IDs and revision. Failed renders preserve native content; reconnect does not duplicate strokes or replay committed changes.

Draft context menus: selected objects expose Copy, Duplicate, Group/Ungroup when valid, layer order, Lock/Unlock, Properties and Delete; background exposes Paste, Insert and view controls; a path point exposes point type, split/add/remove and coordinate editing. Disabled operations explain geometry/lock constraints. All menus preserve the explicit target.

Acceptance: draw with mouse and a supported pressure device, edit a preset, reopen and verify earlier strokes remain unchanged. Pan/zoom then select a shape using the same geometry; move its layer and Undo. Create a path in Canvas, reuse it in Present and edit its anchors without rasterisation. Toggle AI and confirm exactly one options host.
Sources: UX27-CANVAS-001–005; Atlas owner Canvas tool/insert revision; Atlas shared editable-path builder contract;

— Study references canonical Subjects, Topics, paper/specification mappings and owning-app resources. Labels may change without replacing IDs. The desktop navigation retains New Chat, Subjects, My Progress, Planner, Revision Bank, recent chats and at most three Revise These recommendations across all subjects. Rank deterministically: recorded weak topics first, then overdue/oldest-reviewed, with stable TopicID ties; show the reason and fewer than three when eligibility requires.

— Time spent, streaks, resource opens and card flips are engagement, not demonstrated proficiency. Topic states are Not assessed, Needs work, Developing and Confident, derived from attributed answers and review records. Never label an unassessed topic weak/mastered. A learner's self-reported confidence is separate and cannot silently change proficiency or another learner's private evidence.

— Learn/Practise/Test/Review changes the next request within the same Study session, retaining ConversationID, TopicID, history, source selection and answer draft. Preserve meaningful mode-transition provenance. Practise records an actually submitted attempt with question/source, working, feedback, marking provenance and hint conditions. An unanswered displayed question adds no evidence.

— Test uses the canonical Forms Test/Quiz engine and inspectable rules/rubric. Selecting Test alone starts no timer and fabricates no grade. Learn worked examples and Review page opens do not record mastery. My sources only applies the configured closed-corpus rule; Wider knowledge allowed labels supplied sources, external research and general explanation while still respecting web/account permissions. Switching policy never rewrites earlier provenance.

— Revision Bank categories are Recommended, All, Flashcards, Notes, Papers and Quizzes, with Create New at the right. Resource cards reference Cards, Forms and Write artifacts; View/interact is default, editing/Open in App is explicit. Planner opens the canonical Study burrow, and linked topic context follows the composer rather than creating a second content store.

— Cards groups canonical CardIDs/SetIDs without duplicating content. Due counts, total cards, current position and completed reviews are separate measures. Review defaults to a focused vertical stack with shadowed neighbouring cards; the supported horizontal alternative remains available. View flips on activation and cannot edit; Edit uses click-to-edit with an explicit Flip control and never flips from an ordinary content click.

— Front and Back are independently editable structured content with fonts, backgrounds, images/graphs and ink preserved in native save/export. Add, duplicate, reorder, remove/restore and bulk changes retain IDs and recoverable revisions. Set topic links and card metadata are separate from private ReviewRecords; shared content edits never overwrite another learner's ratings.

— Red/amber/green ratings create private attributed review evidence and update a valid linked Study topic. An unlinked card offers topic linking instead of inventing a mapping. New cards remain unassessed. Save conflicts and partial bulk outcomes must be explicit; neither a fixture rating nor a page-open event proves a learning result.

— Read-only sets allow permitted review but prevent content edits; revoked source media shows unavailable. Empty Study has no invented grades or topics. Topic details expose attributed attempts, hint/open-book conditions, last/next review and source links. Ranking/rules are versioned; precise evidence weights, proficiency thresholds and review intervals remain an explicit unresolved product policy in STUDY-UI/AC source, not constants for the implementer to invent. Keyboard card navigation and Flip preserve focus; Edit/View switching preserves the draft.

Draft context menus: resource cards offer View, Open in App, Copy link and permitted organisation actions; topic rows offer evidence/review inspection and topic-bound practice; cards offer Edit, Duplicate, Move, Topic link and Remove. Ratings remain explicit review actions, never decorative menu side effects.

Acceptance: change session mode while drafting an answer, switch source policy, submit one attempt and trace its evidence to the topic. Flip a card without rating and confirm no proficiency change. Rate a linked card and verify only that learner's record changes. Mobile Overview/Subjects/Progress/Bank keeps Planner and full navigation reachable, and the composer stays above keyboard/safe areas.
Sources: STUDY-UI-202/205/210–220; LE-08–10; UX27-SPACES-012; UX27-OTHER-006; Atlas approved Study/Cards contracts;
; V3-CARDS-LAY-01–02; V3-CARDS-FEA-01–03; V3-CARDS-ENT-01–02; V3-SPACES-FEA-21–22; STUDY-UI-203/206/208/217–219; STUDY-AC-211–212;

— Retain the spreadsheet engine: formulas, dependency-aware recalculation, tables, structured fields, filtering, sorting, views and charts. A workbook/database, sheet/table, cell/record and source revision have stable identity. Spreadsheet, database and SQL projections share data only where an explicit mapping exists; changing view never creates parallel records. SQL names the actual connection/runtime. Manual commands, queries and AI mutations remain distinguishable.

— Active cell, selected range and editing are different states. The formula bar shows the active expression; reference tokens map to the corresponding ranges. Anchored function help preserves the edit. Commit/Cancel is explicit; Enter commits into the same cell before normal navigation. Results use actual typed values, errors, locale and units, never fixture success.

— Every AI mutation requires approval of that concrete action, including when general Take actions is enabled. Review identifies source/revision, affected cells or records, proposed diff, validation and recovery. Live-database changes require the applicable backup; failed backup blocks approval. A proposal, approved operation, executed result and failed/partial operation are separate records. Revalidate stale ranges rather than writing into shifted data.

— Chart insertion binds actual ranges, headers, categories and series. Preview is uncommitted; Insert creates one editable chart. Invalid references and empty series are visible. Authored chart colours persist across UI themes; the old green app-accent preference does not override the user's shared palette.

— Retain typed multi-value/structured cells, nested tables with owned-versus-referenced identity, multidimensional DataCubes, slices/pivots and explicit relational projections. These deeper source capabilities are not fully designed by the four spreadsheet mockups; use the complete Data engine contract.

Draft menus/keyboard: cells expose Copy/Paste, Insert/Delete row or column, Format and applicable data operations; charts expose Edit data, Properties and Remove. Selection defines scope. Escape cancels an uncommitted formula; keyboard range navigation must not accidentally submit an AI mutation.

Acceptance: edit/cancel a formula, insert a bound chart, change source data and observe the actual chart update. Attempt an AI write with global Take actions enabled: its concrete approval remains mandatory. Reject a failed-backup write and retain the original data.

— Forms owns canonical FormID/TestID, stable QuestionIDs, sections, answers, validation/branching/scoring rules and versions. Reordering questions preserves branch references. Retain supported answer types, constraints, defaults, typed TableInput/repeating responses, Form/Test/Quiz presets, custom modes over the shared state runtime, and assessment maths/marking rules. The condition/regex tester exposes samples and failures; malformed or unsafe conditions cannot be published as valid.

— Draft, respondent Preview and published version are distinct. Preview opens the selected draft with disposable answers; it neither publishes nor creates a real response. Return to Build preserves draft edits. Publish shows audience/access and exact version; changes to published forms preserve explicit response/version compatibility and response privacy. A real response is accepted only after durable persistence; export of responses is a separate operation.

Draft menus/keyboard: question rows offer Duplicate, Reorder, Required, Branching and Delete with reference checks. Tab reaches question and answer controls in respondent order; builder shortcuts never leak into respondent input. An empty form offers Add question; missing branch targets identify the offending question; a failed submission retains the respondent's answers and a safe retry.

Acceptance: reorder a branched question, preview both paths, cancel preview and compare unchanged response counts. Publish a known revision, submit once, recover a failed save without duplicate responses, and verify Study references that same assessment.
Sources: V3-DATA-FEA-01–04; V3-DATA-ENT-01–02; UX27-DATA-001–004; CUI-PREF-203; V3-FORMS-FEA-01–03; UX27-OTHER-005;

— Files provides provider-native create/open/import, rename, move, copy, trash/restore and metadata through real capabilities. Preserve FileID/provider identity, path, revision and operation receipts. List and Grid show the same folder/selection; address, breadcrumbs, back/forward, search, sorting and details share navigation state. Local availability and provider sync are separate: a cloud outage does not block local folders or turn pending uploads into confirmed remote files.

— Move preserves identity; Copy deliberately creates another artifact. Collision handling offers explicit applicable Replace, Keep both or Skip, with per-item outcomes for bulk operations. Preview/Open in App resolves the owner and permissions. Opening a .9to1board edits the same board; Boards also works without Files installed. Empty folders, denied locations, disconnected providers and unsupported previews have useful alternatives without exposing inaccessible metadata.

— The ten organisation types are Folder, Project, Sheet, Tree, Smart, Timeline, Pipeline, Catalogue, Stash and Matrix. They share nesting/navigation and an ordinary Contents view without erasing specialised state. Tree separates editable visual structure from reader View. Smart queries are source-scoped; Pipeline movement enforces stage/gate rules; Matrix uses stable row/column axes rather than current display positions. Unshown specialised editors remain retained requirements, not completed mockups.

— Sheet arranges references, notes, drawings and shapes. Add existing defaults to Add reference. Removing a placement does not delete or move the source. The default file opening policy is Pop-up; in authoring, click selects and explicit Open enters the item. A source editor discloses when it edits the original. Authored geometry/connectors/opening policy persist; personal selection, viewport and chosen view do not become shared content. This approved Sheet contract supersedes earlier ambiguous spreadsheet-like wording.

Draft menus/keyboard: file rows offer Open, Open in App, Rename, Copy, Move, Share where supported, Details and Trash. F2 renaming, clipboard commands and Delete operate on explicit selection; a specialised placement offers Remove reference separately. Escape returns focus to the invoking row. Acceptance: switch List/Grid, move without breaking links, reject a collision, remove a Sheet placement and reopen its unchanged source.

— Flow is a continuous composed document with one primary vertical scroll. Preserve the report composition example: a Data section, Write content, image, a second section of the same Data source, and a report Assistant. Each placement records source identity, section selection and live/pinned revision policy. Arrange, duplicate placement and remove affect composition; Edit original independently checks source permission and returns to the same Flow position.

— Binder is one authored interconnected document, with nested notes, folders, tabs/stacks, sections, connections and shared objects. It is not a provider-folder copy. Readers navigate through outline, links, breadcrumbs and Back without authoring handles. Closing a container restores viewport/focus. Cancelling Insert leaves no source mutation. Missing/deleted sources, lost permission and newer source revisions remain visible and recoverable.

Draft menus/keyboard: a Flow placement offers Open original, Revision policy, Move, Duplicate placement and Remove placement; Binder objects expose applicable structure and link commands. Keyboard navigation follows reading order; editing commands require author mode. Acceptance: embed two regions of one Data artifact, edit the original, verify both declared revision policies, remove one placement without deleting data, and traverse/return from a Binder container with focus restored.
Sources: V3-FILES-FEA-01–05; V3-FILES-ENT-01–02; TF-F01–F11, especially TF-F04; UX27-FILES-001–004; UX27-BOARD-003–006; V3-LINK-FEA-01–03; TF-L01–03; TF-X01–02;

— Events and PlannerTasks keep stable identity across Day/Week/Month/Agenda, calendars and burrows. Dragging an unscheduled task onto the grid schedules that task without duplicating it. Burrow membership references the source. Task completion differs from dismissing a reminder; removing membership differs from deletion.

— Edit exposes the actual calendar, start/end, timezone, duration and reminder. Recurring edits choose this occurrence, following occurrences or entire series. AI scheduling proposes target calendar, times and conflicts before an authorised commit. Conflicting, unavailable or offline calendars retain the proposal and truthful pending state. An empty calendar is distinct from a failed load.

— The event's category colour is an inset nib with its own radius, not the event border. Collapse secondary panels before shrinking the grid beyond use; Agenda is the narrow alternative. Draft context menus expose Open, Edit, Reschedule, Complete for tasks, recurrence-aware Delete and calendar details. Keyboard alternatives support selecting an event and editing its time without drag precision.

Acceptance: schedule one existing task, open it through Study's canonical burrow and confirm identity; edit one recurrence without changing the series; reject a conflicting AI proposal; switch Agenda/Week without losing selection.

— Automations uses the shared typed Node Graph: trigger, input, condition, action and output nodes, compatible ports, branches, parallelism, approvals, retries and typed app/tool operations. Preserve AutomationID, node IDs and revisions. Draft and Active are different; Save or Test never activates. Validate graph types, dependencies and effective permissions before activation, with errors attached to the offending node/edge.

— Tests name sample input, target environment and live/mock status. A live test retains external-action approvals. Runs pin the starting revision and record each node's actual outcome. Durable waits survive restart; resumption cannot replay already committed effects. Space commands, Assistant schedules and sidebar entries reference the same AutomationID/revision.

— Schedule settings include clock time, timezone, days, daylight-saving and missed/offline-run policy. Use the canonical scheduler/deduplication contract; changing timezone cannot silently create duplicate runs. Missing credentials or unavailable tools pause/fail clearly with recovery; empty graphs provide a valid starting trigger.

Draft menus/keyboard: nodes offer Configure, Duplicate, Disable where valid and Delete; edges expose compatible reconnect/remove commands. Enter opens node details, Escape closes them, and a keyboard route performs every essential graph operation. Activation, Run, Retry and Cancel are distinct commands.

Acceptance: save an invalid graph without activating it, correct the exact error, test with a declared input, activate a known revision and resume a delayed run after restart without repeating its completed side effect. Verify an offline missed schedule follows its selected policy.
Sources: LE-11; UX27-OTHER-001–002; V3-PLANNER-FEA-01–03; UX27-AUTO-001–006; V3-AUTOMATIONS-FEA-01–04;

— Each native media project retains its own ID/revision, editable objects, original media and nondestructive edit history. Project Save is distinct from rendering/export. Missing media/fonts, unsupported decoders, unavailable processing and interrupted jobs preserve the project and expose relink/retry/cancel. A preview image or fixture waveform is never evidence of a real file or successful job.

— Automatic object composition and optional manual layers share one model without flattening. Preserve semantic/manual selections, layers, masks, text, crop/resize, vector/raster transforms, adjustments, ordering, visibility and opacity. Layer and mask are separately selected targets. Painting a mask never erases the original image; size, softness, opacity, visibility and inversion apply to the named mask. Hit testing and rendering use the same image transform. AI edits are revision-bound proposals with provenance and review.

— Export names format, dimensions, colour profile, alpha and destination, rendering actual composition rather than an editor screenshot. Draft layer menus offer Duplicate, Group where valid, Order, Add/Edit mask and Delete; view shortcuts never mutate pixels. Acceptance: edit/undo a mask, relink a missing source and export a known revision with alpha preserved.

— Retain multitrack timeline/mixer, import/record, trim/split/move, fades, gain, automation, effects/bus routing, waveform/spectrogram repair, Enhance Audio, Denoise and mix export. Transport time, source waveforms, levels and recording states come from actual media/backend. Recording requires the selected device grant and armed tracks. Clip source offset, timeline start, duration and gain remain distinct; numeric fade and handle edits update the same envelope.

— Split Stems is a first-class tool: declare source, backend, resource requirements and output tracks; preserve the original and align provenance-linked outputs. Pending/Running/Failed/Complete reflects the actual job. Export uses the selected range, revision and sample rate; unavailable output is not shown as complete.

Draft clip menus offer Split, Trim, Duplicate, Mute, Fades and Relink where applicable. Space controls transport outside text entry; selection movement and audition never overwrite source media. Acceptance: trim a clip, edit its fade numerically, cancel a stem job, successfully retry and compare aligned outputs; reopen the project with edit history intact.

— Media bin, source/program viewer, contextual inspector and multitrack timeline share canonical clip/source identities. Preserve compositing, titles, effects, keyframes, animation, audio alignment and the shared-framework advanced node editor with Motion-specific node families. Playback uses the same frame/timebase as the playhead. At a selected cut, transition effect, duration, alignment and available source handles are explicit; insufficient handles produce a real warning.

— Proxy/preview quality differs from final output. Render review identifies revision, range, format, resolution, frame rate, audio and destination, validating dependencies before queueing. A queue entry, project save and completed output are different states. Draft menus offer Split, Trim, Transition, Properties, Relink and Remove; keyboard frame stepping must match rendered frames. Acceptance: add a valid transition, reject one lacking handles, render a chosen range and verify output duration/audio alignment; failed render leaves editable sources intact.

— Code, Sites and Stacks operate on the same ProjectID, canonical files and revision. Code retains real language services, completion/signatures, navigation, formatting/refactoring, diagnostics, build/test/debug and source control. Diagnostics target actual current file/ranges. AI edits produce typed diffs with validation and applicable approval; proposed terminal execution is separately reviewed against the actual session.

— Code and CUI visual building edit the same model. Invalid hot reload preserves the draft and labels the last valid preview stale. Completion accept/dismiss preserves editor focus; one accepted suggestion is one undo operation. Monospace belongs to code/diagnostics rather than all app chrome. New Project includes the canonical 9to1 Extension type with target/contribution filtering.
